items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I bought Paul Whiteman's records, Ben Bernie's records, and then I got to know all those fellows later on

ctx.x: Oh, of course, sure. I used to -- you

know, I think I told how I used to buy records, everybody's records, you know. If something came out I'd buy it and then during the day, you know, I'd play these records and listen to them, and -- because that was the only way you could pick up on what was happening, you know. I'd buy all the stuff. I bought Paul Whiteman's records, Ben Bernie's records, and then I got to know all those fellows later on and it was -- it was fine. There were a lot of people -- you see, then you'd listen to this man for one thing,…

But in those days if you were a saxophone player you had to play with some kind of tone. You had to have some beauty in your playing, like they say, and if you didn't have it, then you were kaput. Like I remember in Chick Webb's band we had the three saxophone players, Elmer Williams, Hilton Jefferson and myself, and we used to alternate on the playing the lead, you know, because Jeff had a better tone than I did. See, he could play something real pretty and beautiful. So he played the first part, you know. But…
